summary: Chelsea beat Championship side Blackburn 2-0 at Stamford Bridge in the Carabao Cup fourth round, with goals from Benoît Badiashile and Raheem Sterling, to reach the quarter-finals. Cole Palmer was outstanding and involved in both goals, while Reece James returned from injury. Manager Mauricio Pochettino stayed tense throughout despite the comfortable win, and Chelsea will face Newcastle in the last eight.
one_line: Chelsea beat Blackburn 2-0 through Badiashile and Sterling goals, with Cole Palmer outstanding, to reach the Carabao Cup quarter-finals against Newcastle.
key_facts: Chelsea beat Blackburn 2-0 at Stamford Bridge in the Carabao Cup fourth round, with goals from Benoît Badiashile and Raheem Sterling.
Badiashile scored the opener in his first appearance of the season, sidefooting home after goalkeeper Leopold Wahlstedt palmed Conor Gallagher's cross to his feet.
Cole Palmer helped create the opener with a nutmeg and a quickly-taken corner combining with Gallagher, and was involved in Sterling's goal.
Sterling curled in from the edge of the area after Palmer intercepted Callum Brittain's pass as Blackburn tried to play out.
Reece James started for the first time since the opening day of the season after injury; Pochettino called him "one of the best full-backs in the world".

Blackburn manager Jon Dahl Tomasson fielded a young team, with 26-year-old captain Lewis Travis the oldest player; he said it was "the millionaires of the Premier League against the youngsters of the Championship".
Blackburn are 12th in the Championship after an inconsistent start.
Referee Tim Robinson turned down penalty appeals for a Travis challenge on Sterling and for a Brittain cross hitting Gallagher's arm; there was no VAR.
Chelsea fans celebrated only their fourth home win of the season, three of them in the Carabao Cup.
Pochettino faces his first return to table-topping Tottenham on Monday night.
Chelsea will host Newcastle in the quarter-finals, to be played week commencing 18 December.
Other quarter-finals: Everton v Fulham, Port Vale v Middlesbrough, Liverpool v West Ham.
Newcastle reached the last eight by beating Manchester City and then beating Manchester United 3-0 at Old Trafford.
